subject: Reserved Commitment Sizing + Conditional GPU Pass-Through Proposal
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Ng <alyssa@luminaai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved Commitment Sizing + Conditional GPU Pass-Through Proposal

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I wanted to put a concrete first-pass proposal in writing so your procurement team has something to react to. High-level: 

- Proposed reserved capacity: 40 p100-equivalent GPUs (baseline), with the ability to burst to 60 for short periods using our burst pool.
- Term: 12 months optional, with an 18-month alternative if Lumina wants a deeper discount.
- Pricing sensitivity: we are proposing a conditional pass-through clause: if market GPU costs (defined below) increase >12% vs. our reference index, we reserve the right to adjust unit pricing on a pro-rata basis. Conversely, if market GPU costs decline >8%, we will pass through favorable pricing.

Attached: commit_terms_draft.pdf and gpu_cost_scenarios.xlsx (high-level cost model and example pass-through calculations).

Next steps for us: I want to flag internal approval requirements (cc'ing Marissa). If the final effective discounting to Lumina remains <=15% off list, we can typically approve in sales ops. Discounts beyond that will need finance approval and may trigger an exec exception.

Questions for you to help us move faster:
1) Do you have a 12-month utilization forecast (avg. and 95th percentile) so we can size the commit more tightly?
2) Is Lumina comfortable with a market-indexed clause, or would you prefer a fixed-price escalation band?
3) Procurement timeline/target signature date?

If it helps, Marissa can propose a clean set of contract language and the approval path for each discount band.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Director, Strategic Deals
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment stubs: commit_terms_draft.pdf (49 KB), gpu_cost_scenarios.xlsx (320 KB)

From: Alyssa Ng <alyssa@luminaai.com>

Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved Commitment Sizing + Conditional GPU Pass-Through Proposal

Diego —

Thanks for the write-up and the model. A few quick answers and asks from our side:

- Utilization: we can provide a month-by-month forecast; high-level, we expect 55% average utilization on the baseline (with spikes up to ~85% during model retrains). I’ll get the detailed forecast to you by EOD Monday.
- Indexed clause: procurement prefers a symmetric, capped pass-through (e.g., +/- up to 20%), with a quarterly reconciliation window. Can you draft example language that reflects a cap and reconciliation cadence?
- Timeline: procurement’s target is a signed commitment by Apr 15.

Two things we need clarified before committing:
1) What triggers require internal approvals (e.g., discount thresholds, term length)?
2) If market prices spike, what notice period will Redwood provide before adjusting invoiced rates?

Jordan is joining procurement on our side and will be the day-to-day contact (cc’d). Looking forward to Marissa’s note on approvals.

Thanks,
Alyssa Ng
Head of Platform Ops
Lumina AI

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved Commitment Sizing + Conditional GPU Pass-Through Proposal

Alyssa, Diego —

Appreciate the draft, Diego. I’m looping in Ben (Finance) and Karthik (Product/Capacity) to outline the approval path and practical sizing concerns. Below is a pragmatic approval and term playbook that should help procurement plan: 

Approval bands (internal):
- Up to 15% list discount: Sales Manager (me) can greenlight. Standard 12-month tenor.
- 15-18%: Requires Finance manager (Ben) sign-off; we need a utilization guarantee (min committed utilization) or a revenue protection clause.
- 18-25%: Requires Finance + Head of Revenue approval and a dedicated capacity carve-out (to avoid oversubscribe risk).
- >25%: Executive approval (SVP/CEO) + legal approval on custom pass-through wording.

Term vs. price trade-offs:
- 12 months: baseline pricing as proposed.
- 18 months: ~5-8 percentage points additional discount in our models (see pricing_table_v2.csv attached).

Pass-through mechanics (proposal):
- Reference index: a weighted internal GPU price index derived from our supplier contracts and market spot (we'll share the formula).
- Trigger window: quarterly reconciliation, 30-day notice for upward adjustments, pass-through capped at +/- 20% per year.
- Reconciliation: if overcharged/undercharged relative to index, we issue a credit/charge on the next invoice.

Sizing note from Karthik (cc’d): we should avoid sizing purely to peak because burst capacity is available. Recommend firm commit = 35 p100-equivalent with a burst pool to 60; that reduces effective unit costs for Lumina and limits Redwood’s exposure. Karthik, can you confirm if 35 baseline + burst is feasible operationally?

Alyssa — once we agree on approval bands and the pass-through cap, I can route the proposed pricing through finance and mark the deal for expedited review. If Lumina needs deeper discounting tied to an 18-month term, please indicate that explicitly and we’ll start the finance + legal path now.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Lead, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

--

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Reserved Commitment Sizing + Conditional GPU Pass-Through Proposal

All —

Quick finance read: the approval bands Marissa laid out are aligned with our risk tolerances, but a couple of clarifications and asks before we can greenlight anything beyond 15%: 

1) Formal pass-through clause: legal needs specific formula language (index composition, weights, smoothing). We should not leave the "reference index" as a black box. Please push legal-ready language; I can fast-track once drafted.

2) Minimum committed utilization: For any discount >15% we need a minimum monthly utilization guarantee (we typically translate to a $-value or a minimum GPU-hour floor). Procurement should sign to that floor.

3) Escalation & contingency: if GPU supply market shocks >30% in a single quarter, we will need an emergency review and may put a temporary cap on bursts for all dedicated commitments until we rebalance. That scenario will require VP-level sign-off.

4) Approval threshold tweak: based on current budget cycles, anything that effectively reduces annual expected contribution margin by >10% requires Head of Finance + CRO (rather than Head of Revenue). So change 18-25% band to require Finance Head + CRO.

I will review the excel scenarios (gpu_cost_scenarios.xlsx) this afternoon and provide a short memo outlining worst/baseline/best cases and the approval recommendation.

Ben Carter
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
